titulo: Multilingual as a lever: the Spanish case
lead: In Spanish, the competition is usually smaller and the demand is big. On INEMA, the page about learning AI in Spanish was indexed on 10/03/2026, and the following week it was already showing up in queries that the Portuguese version didn't reach. In this lesson, you use data to decide whether a page deserves another language, and how to do it without falling into mass translation.
objetivo: decide, using real countries and queries, whether a winning page deserves a version in another language, and plan that reviewed version.

aprende.t: Reading countries and languages in Search Console
What Spanish showed on INEMA (and what it hasn't shown yet)
Reviewed version, hreflang, and a destination in the language

hero_alt: Two people talk at an outdoor café table in a square, one showing the other their phone.

secoes.titulo: From the clue in the dashboard to the page in the other language

nos.detalhe: In Performance, the Countries tab. Impressions from countries that speak another language show that people are already getting close to your topic.

Each language searches differently. In Spanish, "IA" and "inteligencia artificial" compete; "desde cero" shows up where Portuguese says "do zero". Validate with autocomplete and Search Console, not with the translator.
Translating costs little; the expensive part is reviewing and adapting. Title, address, and examples in the language. A person reviews before publishing, just like in Portuguese.
Each version points to itself as canonical and to the others with hreflang, only between versions that actually exist (course 1, lesson 5).
Without a next step in the visitor's language (course, community, contact), the page educates but doesn't convert. It's the main decision.

secoes.volta: Measured it? The next winning page goes back to the queue
secoes.legenda: Start with a page that has already shown a signal, not the whole site.

texto: Look at the countries by impressions for the last 28 days.
A few impressions from abroad is not ready-made demand; it is a signal to test with one page.

exemplo.texto: Impressions by country: Brazil 1,449, Portugal 106, Argentina 24, Uruguay 13. A small signal, but from people who speak Spanish.

texto: Pick a page that already works in your language and make the version in the other one, with its own title and address.
One well-reviewed page is worth more than ten sloppily translated ones.

exemplo.texto: On 09/30/2026, the target queries in Portuguese sat between positions 23 and 69, with 0 clicks. The page /es/aprender-inteligencia-artificial/ was indexed on 10/03; the following week it had 5 to 10 impressions on each Spanish query, at positions 29 to 61.

texto: A Spanish impression is not a click or a conversion. At INEMA, the case shows that the language opened a door; the click has not come yet.
Measure the new version in the same weekly export, separated by page.
Machine translation published at scale, without review, falls under the scaled content policy.
One page at a time, reviewed, with a destination in the language.

secoes.titulo: The hreflang and the version plan
secoes.sub: Replace what is between < > with your own. The hreflang goes on each page, not in the general layout.

blocos.rot: hreflang on each version (the same lines on all three pages)
blocos.conteudo:
<link rel="alternate" hreflang="pt-BR" href="https://www.<seusite.com>/<pagina-pt>/">
<link rel="alternate" hreflang="es" href="https://www.<seusite.com>/es/<pagina-es>/">
<link rel="alternate" hreflang="en" href="https://www.<seusite.com>/en/<pagina-en>/">
<link rel="alternate" hreflang="x-default" href="https://www.<seusite.com>/<pagina-pt>/">

Source page: </pagina-pt/> (signal: <impressions, queries>)
Language: <es>
Validated query in the language: <query> (autocomplete: yes/no; Search Console: <impressions>)
Title and address in the language: <title> · </es/<slug-no-idioma>/>
Who reviews: <name>
Destination in the language: <course / group / contact in Spanish>
Measurement: weekly export, new page row, for 4 weeks

• 10/03: ES page about learning AI indexed.
  • Week of 10/05 to 10/11: "aprender ia" 10 impressions, "aprender inteligencia artificial desde cero" 10, "cómo aprender ia" 8, positions 29 to 61.

secoes.sub: If the dashboard shows no other language, E2 becomes a justified "not yet."

exercicios.texto: Write down the 5 countries with the most impressions in the last 28 days and any queries in another language that show up.
exercicios.pronto: the list has 5 countries with impressions and the queries in another language (or "none").

exercicios.titulo: E2 · The plan for one version
exercicios.texto: Pick a page with a signal and fill in the version plan: validated query in the language, its own title and address, reviewer, and destination in the language.
exercicios.pronto: the plan has the query checked in autocomplete, who reviews, and a destination in the language; or one sentence with the reason to wait.

secoes.sub: The explanation appears after your answer.

perguntas.p: The INEMA ES page gained Spanish impressions the week after indexing. What does the case prove?
opcoes: That the language opened a door to queries that Portuguese did not reach; the click has not come yet.
That it is better to translate the whole site.
perguntas.explica: Impressions of 5 to 10 per query, at positions 29 to 61, and 0 non-branded clicks on the club. A signal, not a final result.

perguntas.p: Why is it not enough to translate the title word for word?
opcoes: Because each language searches differently: the query must be validated in the language.
Because hreflang does not allow it.
perguntas.explica: "Do zero" becomes "desde cero"; "AI" and "inteligencia artificial" compete. Translation is not keyword research.

perguntas.p: What is the risk of publishing 200 automatically translated pages all at once?
opcoes: Falling under the scaled content policy and not getting indexed.
perguntas.explica: Mass translation without review is treated as scaled content. One page at a time, reviewed.

perguntas.p: The ES page turned out great, but the button leads to a community that is only in Portuguese. What's missing?
opcoes: A destination in the visitor's language: without it, the page educates but doesn't convert.
perguntas.explica: INEMA's own study points to this as the main decision for a version in another language.

itens.texto: Start with the one that already works, not the whole site.
Validate the search in that language; don't trust the translator.
Reviewed by a person, with reciprocal hreflang and a next step in the language.
